author: DTrim99
body:
Two different things here — one by design, one a real bug on our side:

**The $105.74 rebate** is the Chapter 62F taxpayer refund (14.0312% of 2021 net liability, paid November 2022). Per the convention from #1068 (and the timing discussion in #716), PolicyEngine books it to the liability year inside siitax and reports it separately in the `srebate` column, so `compare` scores `siitax + srebate` on both sides — that removes the timing difference against TAXSIM, which books it in the 2022 payout year.

**The $1,000 is a bug — good catch.** It's PolicyEngine's model of the [MA COVID-19 Essential Employee Premium Pay Program](https://www.mass.gov/info-details/covid-19-essential-employee-premium-pay-program) (Ch. 102, Acts of 2021): $500 per qualifying worker (earnings above the minimum and AGI under 300% of poverty), and both spouses qualify on this record. Those were direct checks mailed in 2022 — never a Form 1 line — but the emulator wasn't neutralizing the variable the way we already neutralize Maine's affordability payment. #1065 now zeroes it; that also corrects the 62F base on this record (14.0312% × $1,753.58 = $246.06 instead of $105.74, since the phantom credit was shrinking the rebate base), giving siitax = $1,507.52 with srebate = $246.06.

```
taxsimid,year,state,mstat,page,sage,depx,pwages,swages,intrec,idtl
4204822,2021,22,2,63,61,0,20952.381,23047.619,3437.6497,5
```

On the remaining pre-credit gap vs TaxAct's $1,932: your TaxAct return didn't take the automatic line 11a/11b deduction for Social Security/Medicare paid ($3,366 × 5% ≈ $168 — probably because no W-2 detail was entered; both taxsimtest and PE apply it), and PE currently grants the $200 Massachusetts-bank-interest exemption to generic `intrec` ($10) — arguably it shouldn't, since TAXSIM's interest isn't necessarily Mass-bank interest. TaxAct's $3,516 bottom line also includes a $1,584 Schedule HC healthcare penalty that neither TAXSIM nor PE models.
